title: On the Necessity of World Knowledge for Mitigating Missing Labels in Extreme Classification

problem.claim: Extreme classification systems learn query-document relevance from implicit-feedback datasets that often contain missing labels, resulting in missing knowledge needed to model relevance.

gap.claim: Existing propensity-weighting and data-imputation methods that rely solely on the training dataset are hard-pressed to recover the missing knowledge, while directly using large language models is challenging under low-latency and large-document-set requirements.

contributions.claim: The authors propose SKIM, a scalable algorithm combining small language models with abundant unstructured metadata to address missing labels.
The authors formally show that missing knowledge caused by systematic missing labels is difficult to recover using existing training-data-only methods.
The authors release SKIM code and trained models.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that SKIM outperforms existing methods on Recall@100 by more than 10 absolute points.
The authors report that SKIM outperforms baseline methods by 12% in offline evaluations on proprietary query-ad retrieval data with 10 million documents.
The authors report a 1.23% increase in ad click-yield in an online A/B test on Bing Search.

narrative_sequence.summary: Extreme classification maps queries to relevant documents in very large document sets and commonly learns from implicit feedback.
Implicit-feedback datasets often have missing labels, which produce missing knowledge relevant to query-document relevance modeling.
Training-data-only recovery methods are insufficient, and large language models are difficult to deploy at the required scale and latency.
SKIM combines small language models with unstructured metadata to infuse missing knowledge at scale.
The authors report gains on public and proprietary datasets, including offline and online evaluations.

source_observation.claim: Systematic missing labels can create missing knowledge that training-data-only correction methods cannot readily recover.

interpretation.claim: When labels are systematically absent, improving relevance modeling may require information sources beyond the observed feedback data.

application.claim: For large-scale retrieval systems, consider combining external metadata with smaller language models when mitigating missing-label effects.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach is effective for domains, latency targets, or data conditions outside those evaluated by the authors.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify SKIM's detailed algorithmic steps or training procedure.
The abstract does not identify the public datasets, baselines, or evaluation protocols in detail.
The abstract does not provide statistical uncertainty or independent verification of the reported results.
